In mathematics, the '''Tricomi–Carlitz polynomials''' or '''(Carlitz–) Karlin–McGregor polynomials''' are polynomials studied by Tricomi (1951),<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tricomi |first=Francesco G. |date=December 1951 |title=A class of non-orthogonal polynomials related to those of Laguerre |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02790089 |journal=[[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]] |language=en |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=209–231 |doi=10.1007/BF02790089 |issn=0021-7670|url-access=subscription }}</ref> {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Leonard Carlitz|last=Carlitz|year=1958}},<ref>{{Citation |last1=Carlitz |first1=Leonard |title=On some polynomials of Tricomi |journal=Boll. Un. Mat. Ital. (3) |volume=13 |pages=58–64 |year=1958 |mr=0103303}}</ref> and {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Samuel Karlin|last=Karlin|last2=McGregor|author2-link=James Lewin McGregor|year=1959}},<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Karlin |first=Samuel |last2=McGregor |first2=James |date=1959-03-01 |title=Random walks |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/illinois-journal-of-mathematics/volume-3/issue-1/Random-walks/10.1215/ijm/1255454999.full |journal=Illinois Journal of Mathematics |volume=3 |issue=1 |doi=10.1215/ijm/1255454999 |issn=0019-2082}}</ref> related to [[random walk]]s on the [[positive integers]].

They are given in terms of [[Laguerre polynomials]] by 
:<math> \ell_n(x)=(-1)^nL_n^{(x-n)}(x).</math>

They are special cases of the [[Chihara–Ismail polynomials]].
